passages.text: Jacob resumed his journey and came to the land of the people of the east.
passages.sermon: Jacob was traveling.\r\nHe continued his journey.\r\nHe went to the land of the people of the east.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב רַגְלָ֑יו וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אַ֥רְצָה בְנֵי־ קֶֽדֶם׃

passages.text: He looked and saw a well in the field, and near it lay three flocks of sheep, because the sheep were watered from this well. And a large stone covered the mouth of the well.
passages.sermon:
Jacob traveled to the land of the people of the east.
Jacob looked into the field.
Jacob saw a well in the field.
Three flocks of sheep lay near the well.
The shepherds watered the sheep from this well.
A large stone covered the mouth of the well.
passages.original: וַיַּ֞רְא וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְאֵ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה־ שָׁ֞ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶדְרֵי־ צֹאן֙ רֹבְצִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֚י מִן־ הַבְּאֵ֣ר הַהִ֔וא יַשְׁק֖וּ הָעֲדָרִ֑ים וְהָאֶ֥בֶן גְּדֹלָ֖ה עַל־ פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵֽר׃

passages.text: When all the flocks had been gathered there, the shepherds would roll away the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.
passages.sermon:
All the flocks gathered at the well.
The shepherds rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well.
The shepherds gave water to the sheep.
The shepherds put the stone back over the mouth of the well.
They returned the stone to its place.
passages.original: וְנֶאֶסְפוּ־ שָׁ֣מָּה כָל־ הָעֲדָרִ֗ים וְגָלֲל֤וּ אֶת־ הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וְהִשְׁק֖וּ אֶת־ הַצֹּ֑אן וְהֵשִׁ֧יבוּ אֶת־ הָאֶ֛בֶן עַל־ פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִמְקֹמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: “My brothers,” Jacob asked the shepherds, “where are you from?” “We are from Haran,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jacob saw some shepherds.
Jacob spoke to the shepherds.
Jacob called them “my brothers.”
Jacob asked, “Where are you from?”
The shepherds answered Jacob.
The shepherds said, “We are from Haran.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב אַחַ֖י מֵאַ֣יִן אַתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵחָרָ֖ן אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

passages.text: “Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?” Jacob asked. “We know him,” they replied.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to the shepherds.
Jacob asked a question.
Jacob said, “Do you know Laban?”
Jacob described Laban as the grandson of Nahor.
The shepherds answered Jacob.
The shepherds said, “We know him.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ לָבָ֣ן בֶּן־ נָח֑וֹר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יָדָֽעְנוּ׃

passages.text: “Is he well?” Jacob inquired. “Yes,” they answered, “and here comes his daughter Rachel with his sheep.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to the shepherds.
Jacob asked about Laban.
Jacob said, “Is Laban well?”
The shepherds answered Jacob.
The shepherds said, “Laban is well.”
The shepherds pointed to Rachel.
Rachel is Laban’s daughter.
Rachel was coming.
Rachel was bringing Laban’s sheep.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָהֶ֖ם הֲשָׁל֣וֹם ל֑וֹ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ שָׁל֔וֹם וְהִנֵּה֙ רָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ בָּאָ֖ה עִם־ הַצֹּֽאן׃

passages.text: “Look,” said Jacob, “it is still broad daylight; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to the shepherds.
Jacob said, “It is still broad daylight.
It is not yet time to gather the livestock.
Water the sheep.
Take the sheep back to pasture.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵ֥ן עוֹד֙ הַיּ֣וֹם גָּד֔וֹל לֹא־ עֵ֖ת הֵאָסֵ֣ף הַמִּקְנֶ֑ה הַשְׁק֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן וּלְכ֥וּ רְעֽוּ׃

passages.text: But they replied, “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep.”
passages.sermon:
The men answered Jacob.
They said, “We cannot water the sheep now.
We must wait until all the flocks are gathered here.
We must also wait until someone rolls the stone away from the mouth of the well.
After that, we will water the sheep.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לֹ֣א נוּכַל֒ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֲדָרִ֔ים וְגָֽלֲלוּ֙ אֶת־ הָאֶ֔בֶן מֵעַ֖ל פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֑ר וְהִשְׁקִ֖ינוּ הַצֹּֽאן׃

passages.text: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was still speaking with the men at the well.
Rachel arrived at the well.
Rachel brought her father’s sheep with her.
Rachel was a shepherdess.
passages.original: עוֹדֶ֖נּוּ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֑ם וְרָחֵ֣ל׀ בָּ֗אָה עִם־ הַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י רֹעָ֖ה הִֽוא׃

passages.text: As soon as Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, with Laban’s sheep, he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Rebekah.
Rebekah was the sister of Laban.
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Rachel was with her father’s sheep at the well.
Jacob saw Rachel.
Jacob saw the sheep that belonged to Laban.
Jacob walked up to the well.
A large stone covered the mouth of the well.
Jacob rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well.
Jacob gave water to the sheep that belonged to Laban.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ רָאָ֨ה יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־ רָחֵ֗ל בַּת־ לָבָן֙ אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֔וֹ וְאֶת־ צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיָּ֤גֶל אֶת־ הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיַּ֕שְׁקְ אֶת־ צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept aloud.
passages.sermon: Jacob kissed Rachel.\r\nJacob raised his voice.\r\nJacob wept loudly.
passages.original: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְרָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־ קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ׃

passages.text: He told Rachel that he was Rebekah’s son, a relative of her father, and she ran and told her father.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Rachel.
Jacob said, “I am your father’s relative.”
Jacob said, “I am the son of Rebekah.”
Rachel heard Jacob’s words.
Rachel ran to her father.
Rachel told her father what Jacob said.
passages.original: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד יַעֲקֹ֜ב לְרָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י אֲחִ֤י אָבִ֙יהָ֙ ה֔וּא וְכִ֥י בֶן־ רִבְקָ֖ה ה֑וּא וַתָּ֖רָץ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד לְאָבִֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him all that had happened.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Jacob was the son of Laban’s sister, Rebekah.
Laban heard that Jacob, his sister’s son, had arrived.
Laban ran to meet Jacob.
Laban hugged Jacob.
Laban kissed Jacob.
Laban brought Jacob into his house.
Jacob told Laban everything that had happened.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ לָבָ֜ן אֶת־ שֵׁ֣מַע׀ יַעֲקֹ֣ב בֶּן־ אֲחֹת֗וֹ וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיְחַבֶּק־ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַשֶּׁק־ ל֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר לְלָבָ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: Then Laban declared, “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.” After Jacob had stayed with him a month, Laban said to him, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, “You are my own flesh and blood.”
Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.
After a month, Laban spoke to Jacob again.
Laban said, “You are my relative.”
Laban asked, “Should you work for me without pay?”
Laban said, “Tell me what your wages should be.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לָבָ֔ן אַ֛ךְ עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עִמּ֖וֹ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב הֲכִי־ אָחִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וַעֲבַדְתַּ֖נִי חִנָּ֑ם הַגִּ֥ידָה לִּ֖י מַה־ מַּשְׂכֻּרְתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.
passages.sermon:
Laban was a man.
Laban had two daughters.
The older daughter was named Leah.
The younger daughter was named Rachel.
passages.original: וּלְלָבָ֖ן שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם הַגְּדֹלָה֙ לֵאָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה רָחֵֽל׃

passages.text: Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
passages.sermon:
Leah was the older daughter of Laban.
Leah had weak eyes.
Rachel was the younger daughter of Laban.
Rachel was shapely.
Rachel was beautiful.
passages.original: וְעֵינֵ֥י לֵאָ֖ה רַכּ֑וֹת וְרָחֵל֙ הָֽיְתָ֔ה יְפַת־ תֹּ֖אַר וִיפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Since Jacob loved Rachel, he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob loved Rachel.
Rachel was Laban’s younger daughter.
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “I will serve you for seven years.”
Jacob said, “I will serve for your younger daughter Rachel.”
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־ רָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶֽעֱבָדְךָ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים בְּרָחֵ֥ל בִּתְּךָ֖ הַקְּטַנָּֽה׃

passages.text: Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.”
passages.sermon:
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, “It is better that I give Rachel to you than to another man.”
Laban told Jacob, “Stay here with me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֗ן ט֚וֹב תִּתִּ֣י אֹתָ֣הּ לָ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר שְׁבָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.
passages.sermon:
Jacob loved Rachel.
Jacob agreed to work for seven years to marry Rachel.
Jacob served Laban for seven years.
The seven years felt like only a few days to Jacob.
Jacob felt this way because he loved Rachel.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ד יַעֲקֹ֛ב בְּרָחֵ֖ל שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ בְעֵינָיו֙ כְּיָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֔ים בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete, and I want to sleep with her.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob worked for Laban for seven years to marry Rachel.
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “Give me my wife.”
Jacob said, “My time is finished.”
Jacob said, “I want to be with her.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב אֶל־ לָבָן֙ הָבָ֣ה אֶת־ אִשְׁתִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָלְא֖וּ יָמָ֑י וְאָב֖וֹאָה אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Rachel and Leah’s father.
Laban lived in that place.
Laban gathered all the men who lived there.
Laban prepared a feast for them.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף לָבָ֛ן אֶת־ כָּל־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.
passages.sermon:
Laban was the father of Leah.
Evening came.
Laban took his daughter Leah.
Laban brought Leah to Jacob.
Jacob slept with Leah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ לֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אֵלָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.
passages.sermon:
Laban was the father of Leah.
Laban had a female servant named Zilpah.
Laban gave Zilpah to his daughter Leah.
Zilpah became Leah’s maidservant.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לָ֔הּ אֶת־ זִלְפָּ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לְלֵאָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ שִׁפְחָֽה׃

passages.text: When morning came, there was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob said to Laban. “Wasn’t it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob worked for Laban to marry Rachel.
Laban was Jacob’s uncle.
Jacob expected to marry Rachel.
Morning came.
Jacob saw Leah with him.
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “What have you done to me?”
Jacob said, “I served you for Rachel.”
Jacob said, “Why did you deceive me?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּה־ הִ֖וא לֵאָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ לָבָ֗ן מַה־ זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לִּ֔י הֲלֹ֤א בְרָחֵל֙ עָבַ֣דְתִּי עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה רִמִּיתָֽנִי׃

passages.text: Laban replied, “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban was Leah and Rachel’s father.
Laban said, “We do not do that here.”
Laban said, “In our place, we do not give the younger daughter in marriage before the older daughter.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן לֹא־ יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בִּמְקוֹמֵ֑נוּ לָתֵ֥ת הַצְּעִירָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַבְּכִירָֽה׃

passages.text: Finish this week’s celebration, and we will give you the younger one in return for another seven years of work.”
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban was Rachel and Leah’s father.
Laban said, “Finish this week’s celebration.”
Laban promised, “We will give you Rachel also.”
Laban required, “You must work for me another seven years.”
Jacob would receive Rachel after the week.
Jacob must serve Laban for seven more years.
passages.original: מַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וְנִתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ גַּם־ אֶת־ זֹ֗את בַּעֲבֹדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמָּדִ֔י ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־ שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And Jacob did just that. He finished the week’s celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob wanted to marry Rachel.
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Laban told Jacob to finish the week’s celebration.
Jacob obeyed Laban.
Jacob finished the week’s celebration.
After that, Laban gave Rachel to Jacob.
Rachel became Jacob’s wife.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יַעֲקֹב֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיְמַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֛וֹ אֶת־ רָחֵ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Laban had a servant girl named Bilhah.
Laban gave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel.
Bilhah became Rachel’s maidservant.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ אֶת־ בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לָ֖הּ לְשִׁפְחָֽה׃

passages.text: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob married Rachel.
Jacob also slept with Rachel.
Jacob loved Rachel.
Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah.
Laban was Rachel’s father.
Jacob worked for Laban.
Jacob worked for Laban for another seven years.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ גַּ֣ם אֶל־ רָחֵ֔ל וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב גַּֽם־ אֶת־ רָחֵ֖ל מִלֵּאָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמּ֔וֹ ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־ שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
passages.sermon: The LORD saw that Leah was unloved.\r\nThe LORD opened Leah’s womb.\r\nRachel could not have children.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ שְׂנוּאָ֣ה לֵאָ֔ה וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־ רַחְמָ֑הּ וְרָחֵ֖ל עֲקָרָֽה׃

passages.text: And Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”
passages.sermon:
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah.
Leah felt unloved.
Leah became pregnant.
Leah gave birth to a son.
Leah named her son Reuben.
Leah said, “The LORD has seen my suffering.”
Leah said, “Now my husband will love me.”
passages.original: וַתַּ֤הַר לֵאָה֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ רְאוּבֵ֑ן כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֗ה כִּֽי־ רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּעָנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה יֶאֱהָבַ֥נִי אִישִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” So she named him Simeon.
passages.sermon:
Leah was unloved by her husband Jacob.
The LORD saw that Leah was unloved.
Leah conceived again.
Leah gave birth to a son.
Leah said, “The LORD has heard that I am unloved.”
Leah said, “The LORD has given me this son also.”
Leah named her son Simeon.
passages.original: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ שְׂנוּאָ֣ה אָנֹ֔כִי וַיִּתֶּן־ לִ֖י גַּם־ אֶת־ זֶ֑ה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Once again Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So he was named Levi.
passages.sermon:
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Leah conceived again.
Leah gave birth to a son.
Leah said, “Now my husband will be attached to me.”
She said this because she had given Jacob three sons.
Leah named the son Levi.
passages.original: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֤ה הַפַּ֙עַם֙ יִלָּוֶ֤ה אִישִׁי֙ אֵלַ֔י כִּֽי־ יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים עַל־ כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־ שְׁמ֖וֹ לֵוִֽי׃

passages.text: And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. Then Leah stopped having children.
passages.sermon:
Leah was the wife of Jacob.
Leah conceived again.
She gave birth to a son.
Leah said, “This time I will praise the LORD.”
She named her son Judah.
After this, Leah stopped having children.
passages.original: וַתַּ֨הַר ע֜וֹד וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֗ן וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַפַּ֙עַם֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה עַל־ כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד מִלֶּֽדֶת׃
